text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps both you and your teammates work faster. One key habit is following naming conventions: use clear, descriptive names for variables and functions so their purpose is obvious. Another important idea is keeping functions small and focused on a single task. This makes them easier to test and reuse. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because when problems appear, you can find and fix them quickly. In short, writing clean code saves time and reduces mistakes in the long run.
